title: DO NOT BE AFRAID — RISE AGAIN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged. Take the whole army with you, and go up and attack Ai. For I have delivered into your hands the king of Ai, his people, his city and his land. You shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may carry off their plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city." — Josh 8:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the painful defeat at Ai and the dealing with Achan's sin, God speaks tenderly to a shaken Joshua: "Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged." What grace this is. Israel had just failed. They had sinned, been defeated, and buried their dead. And now God does not scold Joshua endlessly or leave him in the dust of that failure. Once the sin was dealt with, God says, "Rise up and go again."

This is one of the most encouraging truths in the whole Bible: failure is not final with God. Once sin is confessed and cleared, God restores His people and calls them forward again. The same city that had defeated them would now fall to them. Where they had known defeat, God would give victory. Our God is the God of second chances.

Notice too the assurance: "I have delivered into your hands the king of Ai." Once again God speaks the victory as already done. This time, though, Israel goes forward not in careless self-confidence but in humbled dependence, having learned the cost of sin.

If you have failed, if you feel defeated and discouraged, hear these words as God's word to you. In Christ, "there is now no condemnation" (Rom 8:1). God does not define you by your worst moment. When Peter denied Jesus, the Lord restored him and sent him out again (John 21:15-17). The God who lifts the fallen is calling you to rise, be forgiven, and move forward. Do not be afraid. Do not be discouraged.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a failure that is keeping you paralysed with fear or discouragement?
2. Do you believe God is truly a God of second chances for you?
3. How does "no condemnation in Christ" free you to rise and move forward?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that failure is not final with You. Where I have fallen, lift me up. Free me from fear and discouragement, and help me rise and go again. Amen.
